newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-KEY WINS 10TH AS ORIOLES ROUT TIGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-KEY WINS 10TH AS ORIOLES ROUT TIGERS.

text.p: Jimmy Key became the second 12-game winner in the American League and Jeffrey Hammonds homered and drove in four runs as the Baltimore Orioles won their fourth straight, 10-1 over the Detroit Tigers Thursday.

Key (12-3) gave up five hits over eight innings, walked two and struck out three to end a personal three-game losing streak. Key, who joined Toronto's Roger Clemens with 12 victories, almost didn't make the start due to a hamstring injury suffered in his last outing on Saturday.
"It didn't bother me, I wasn't really worried about my leg," Key said.
"I threw 22 of 29 hitters strike one."

"Jimmy gave us just what we needed and we showed some signs of life from the offence," Orioles manager Davey Johnson said. "That's great, it was nice to see the offence wake up for him. It really helps Jimmy too because he can be more aggressive."
Hammonds tied a career high with his four RBI.

"I was just glad to get out ahead because Jimmy's one of the best at keeping a lead, that's what he did," Hammonds said. "You can't tell if he's 22-0 or 0-22, he doesn't put any extra pressure on himself or on anyone else. It was just one of those days where I got a couple of pitches I could get the barrel on and then we had some guys on base."
The Orioles have outscored the Tigers 24-5 in winning all four games this season and have taken the last 10 meetings between the teams, including seven in a row at Tiger Stadium.
Detroit had its three-game winning streak snapped.
"We had our butts handed to us tonight," Tigers manager Buddy Bell said. "Key is tough in a 1-0 game, let alone a 7-0 game."
Felipe Lira (5-5) was tagged for a season-high nine runs and 12 hits in seven innings and fell to 1-6 lifetime against the Orioles.
Raul Casanova accounted for the Tigers' offence with his fourth home run in the eighth inning.

In Milwaukee, Brad Radke won his sixth straight start, allowing three runs and four hits over seven innings, and Paul Molitor had two hits, two RBI and two runs scored as the Minnesota Twins snapped a four-game skid with an 8-5 victory over the Brewers.
Radke (10-5) retired 13 consecutive batters before Kelly Stinnett doubled with two out in the fifth inning.
Molitor had an RBI double in the fourth and hit his fourth homer of the season in the ninth for Minnesota, which scored just two runs in a three-game sweep by the Cardinals.

The 40-year-old Molitor also scored a hustle run from third in the fourth inning when catcher Stinnett threw the ball over pitcher Jeff D'Amico's head and Molitor raced home, beating shortstop Jose Valentin's throw
Rick Aguilera pitched the final 1 2/3 innings for his 16th save of the season and his 200th as a member of the Twins.
D'Amico (6-4) lost for the first time in five starts.
Minnesota hit three solo homers, running its streak to 13 homers with none on base.

In Chicago, Aaron Sele tossed a seven-hitter for his first complete-game victory in over three years and Nomar Garciaparra hit a leadoff homer and scored the go-ahead run in a three-run sixth inning as the Boston Red Sox beat the White Sox 4-1.
Sele (10-6) struck out six without a walk to win for the fourth time in his last five decisions.
Garciaparra hit his 13th homer leading off against White Sox starter Doug Drabek (6-6). He tied the Boston record for homers in a season by a rookie shortstop, set by Rico Petrocelli in 1965.
In Toronto, David Wells allowed one run and five hits over 7 1/3 innings and Joe Girardi had three hits and an RBI to lead the New York Yankees to a 3-1 victory over the Blue Jays.
Wells (9-4), a former Blue Jay, walked three and struck out six as the Yankees tied a season high with their fourth straight road win.
Wells recorded 20 first-pitch strikes out of the 29 batters he faced.
Jeff Nelson and Mike Stanton each recorded a strikeout to end the eighth and Mariano Rivera pitched the ninth to earn his major-league leading 27th save.
